editorNote: The week before Thanksgiving finds Atari selling both a renamed 2600 and the new 5200, while Activision-style cartridge energy and vector-console curiosity make the game counter the liveliest corner of the computer store.
morningLine: A black Atari 2600 nameplate, Carol Shaw's River Raid, and a built-in-vector Vectrex give holiday shoppers plenty to compare before they ever reach the office-software shelf.

lead.headline: Atari Puts the 2600 Name on the VCS Era
lead.summary: In November 1982, Atari recast the long-running Video Computer System as the Atari 2600 while the 5200 SuperSystem arrived for the holiday market. The renamed four-switch console kept the older cartridge library visible just as ColecoVision, Intellivision, Vectrex, and Atari's own 5200 pressed shoppers toward newer hardware.
lead.confidence: Month-specific November 1982 rename and 5200 launch; exact store timing varies by account.

computerItems.label: Cartridge Desk
computerItems.headline: River Raid Gives Activision a Fast Holiday Flyer
computerItems.summary: Carol Shaw's River Raid, released for the Atari VCS/2600 in 1982, turns the screen into a vertically scrolling river run of fuel depots, bridges, and enemy craft. By late 1982 it fit the season's best story: third-party VCS games could still feel new even as new consoles arrived.
computerItems.confidence: 1982 release context; November shelf emphasis inferred from late-1982 cartridge coverage.

computerItems.label: Console Counter
computerItems.headline: Atari 5200 Lands Beside Its Older Sibling
computerItems.summary: The 5200 SuperSystem reached shelves in November with Atari 8-bit computer-derived hardware, analog controllers, and a higher suggested price than the older VCS line.
computerItems.confidence: Month-specific November 1982 console launch and period price summary.

computerItems.label: Vector Screen
computerItems.headline: Vectrex Makes the Television Optional
computerItems.summary: General Consumer Electronics' Vectrex also joined the 1982 console field with its own monochrome vector display and color overlays, a striking pitch for families whose television was already booked.

market.headline: Game Hardware Splits the Holiday Pitch
market.summary: Retailers can sell continuity and novelty at once: the renamed Atari 2600 keeps the huge VCS cartridge library alive, the 5200 promises a premium Atari step-up, and Vectrex brings a screen of its own.
